description: Shadow replay of the agent loop: the bytes of each model call and what each tool does are scripted by hand; `expected` is what Super Chat's runAgent (OpenAI Chat Completions adapter) did with them. See docs/AGENT-LOOP.md section 10.

scenarios.name: text-only-streamed
scenarios.description: One model call, text in three fragments, usage in its own final chunk.

scenarios.name: tool-then-answer
scenarios.description: The arguments arrive in two fragments; the tool result goes back; the second call answers.

scenarios.name: text-before-tool-call
scenarios.description: The model says something and then calls a tool; the assistant message keeps both, text first.

scenarios.name: parallel-calls-interleaved
scenarios.description: Two calls whose fragments interleave by index; the second tool finishes first, so tool-result events come in completion order and the history in call order.

scenarios.name: name-and-id-on-later-fragments
scenarios.description: The tool name is split across fragments and the id arrives after the first fragment (the first one is positional only).

scenarios.name: call-without-id-gets-positional-id
scenarios.description: A server that sends no tool call id: the call is named call_<index> and the result is matched to it.

scenarios.name: repaired-arguments
scenarios.description: Arguments in a markdown fence with a trailing comma: repaired, flagged, run.

scenarios.name: unrepairable-arguments
scenarios.description: Arguments that cannot be repaired: the call goes on with what the repair left, and the tool answers for itself.

scenarios.name: unknown-tool
scenarios.description: A tool the host never declared: answered by the loop itself, the model sees what is available.

scenarios.name: tool-name-with-router-prefix
scenarios.description: A router that prefixes the tool name (default_api:echo): TypeScript's registry still finds the tool.

scenarios.name: tool-throws
scenarios.description: A tool that throws is a result with a failure, not an error: the run goes on and the model reads it.

scenarios.name: output-key-order-and-strings
scenarios.description: Tool output with keys out of alphabetical order, nested values and non-ASCII text, and one tool whose output is a plain string: the request body carries them exactly as JSON.stringify writes them.

scenarios.name: tools-listed-in-locale-order
scenarios.description: Tools registered in a jumbled order are declared to the model in localeCompare order (not byte order): punctuation, digits, then letters, lowercase before uppercase.

scenarios.name: frames-after-done-are-ignored
scenarios.description: Nothing after the [DONE] sentinel counts, even a well-formed frame.

scenarios.name: usage-with-details
scenarios.description: Cached input tokens and reasoning tokens ride along in the usage of the step and of the run.

scenarios.name: tool-throws-timeout-and-network
scenarios.description: A thrown error's kind is read from its words: a timeout and a network failure are told apart from the rest.

scenarios.name: confirm-approved
scenarios.description: A confirm tool in an interactive run: the card is announced, the person says yes, the tool runs.

scenarios.name: confirm-declined
scenarios.description: The person says no: the tool does not run, the model reads that, the run goes on.

scenarios.name: confirm-without-a-person
scenarios.description: A confirm tool in a run that cannot ask: denied at once, the tool never runs.

output.error: "send" needs the user's approval and this host cannot ask for it.

messages.content: {"error":"\"send\" needs the user's approval and this host cannot ask for it."}

scenarios.name: step-limit
scenarios.description: The model keeps calling a tool; maxSteps 2 ends the run with the step-limit notice.

scenarios.name: stop-after-tool
scenarios.description: stopWhen afterTool: the run ends after that tool, with finishReason stop and no further model call.

scenarios.name: finish-length-no-usage
scenarios.description: The model is cut off by its output limit and reports no usage.

scenarios.name: stream-ends-without-finish-reason
scenarios.description: The stream ends after the text with no finish_reason and no [DONE]: finishes as stop.

scenarios.name: sse-framing
scenarios.description: CRLF line ends, comment lines, a data field split over two lines, an event named by an event: line, a malformed frame, and frames cut mid-line.

scenarios.name: utf8-split-across-reads
scenarios.description: A multi-byte character cut in half between two reads of the body.

scenarios.name: http-401
scenarios.description: The provider refuses the key: one error event naming the provider's own message.

scenarios.name: http-429-text-body
scenarios.description: A rate limit whose body is not JSON: the body text is the message.

scenarios.name: http-400-context-length
scenarios.description: A 400 whose message names the context window is context-length, not invalid-request.

error.message: This model's maximum context length is 8192 tokens.
This model's maximum context length is 8192 tokens.

scenarios.name: http-500-on-second-step
scenarios.description: The second model call fails: the first step's usage and tool result stand, the run ends in error.

scenarios.name: content-filter-message
scenarios.description: An error whose message mentions a content filter is classified as content-filter whatever the status.

scenarios.name: history-with-earlier-turns
scenarios.description: Earlier turns in the history: a user message with two text parts, an assistant message with a tool call that was answered, and one that was not (dropped from the request).
